data.taskBrief:
TASK BRIEF: Export a Digital Assistant archive to Object Storage (Oracle Digital Assistant Service)

FIT
  Partially. The supplied request exports a Digital Assistant archive to Object Storage, but it does not specify or control a cold/archive storage tier, so it cannot ensure the file is placed in cold object storage.

AUTH
  No authentication scheme is present in the supplied request or collection context. Provide any authentication required by the Oracle API separately.

BASE URL
  https://digitalassistant-api.{{region}}.oci.oraclecloud.com/20190506
  Replace {{region}} with the OCI region identifier; the collection supplies no value for it.

STEPS
  1. POST /odaInstances/:odaInstanceId/digitalAssistants/:digitalAssistantId/actions/export
     Params (JSON body and path):
       odaInstanceId: string — 'oda-instance-ocid' — required path variable identifying the Digital Assistant instance.
       digitalAssistantId: string — 'digital-assistant-id' — required path variable identifying the Digital Assistant.
       target.regionId.value: string — 'us-phoenix-1' — required JSON body field identifying the Object Storage region.
       target.compartmentId.value: string — 'ocid1.compartment.oc1..example' — required JSON body field identifying the Object Storage compartment.
       target.namespaceName.value: string — 'example_namespace' — required JSON body field containing the Object Storage namespace.
       target.bucketName.value: string — 'digital-assistant-exports' — required JSON body field containing the destination bucket name.
       target.objectName.value: string — 'exports/assistant.zip' — required JSON body field containing the destination object name.
       Content-Type: 'application/json' — required request header.
       Accept: 'application/json' — request header shown by the schema.
       opc-request-id: string — optional tracing/request identifier; the saved request marks it disabled.
     Returns:
       202 Accepted with an empty body and response headers opc-request-id and opc-work-request-id. Error examples include 400, 401, 404, 429, and 500; their JSON bodies contain code and message strings.
     Threading:
       None

GOTCHAS
  - Send the body as JSON with the required target nesting; each destination property is represented under a value field in the supplied schema.
  - Replace the unresolved {{region}} in the base URL with the OCI region; no collection value is provided.
  - A successful export is asynchronous: capture opc-work-request-id for operation-status tracking, although no status-query request is supplied here.
  - The request targets Object Storage but exposes no storage-tier/archive-class field, so cold storage placement must be configured elsewhere or after export.
